verdicts.reason: Describes conversion via DGCL §266/TBOC and Plan of Conversion, not an asset sale.
Separates Proposal Three conversion from Proposal Four 2018 award ratification.
Describes Special Committee process and Board recommendation as proxy disclosures, not judicial findings.
Notes Mr. Musk and Kimbal Musk recused themselves from the Board conversion decision.
Identifies Proposal Three’s majority-of-outstanding-shares-entitled-to-vote requirement from p.171.
Identifies the additional non-Musk/Kimbal voting-power requirement and distinguishes the committee’s votes-cast recommendation.
Treats Texas documents as proposed, notes no vote result/effectiveness shown, and identifies approval/filing steps.
Repeatedly distinguishes current Delaware instruments, proposed Texas instruments, and TBOC defaults.
States the Texas two-thirds default and that the proposed charter selects a majority standard where permitted.
Applies the proposed Texas Charter’s majority standard for fundamental transactions rather than only the statutory default.
States current Delaware vacancy filling is by remaining directors or sole director, not stockholders.
States proposed Texas Bylaws allow vacancy filling in any TBOC-permitted manner, including broader methods.
Notes the TBOC limit on filling more than two newly created seats between annual meetings without shareholder action.
Does not assert that conversion by itself declassifies the board or makes all directors annually elected.
Does not apply the proposed Texas Charter’s for-cause removal protection and instead treats director removal as unresolved.
Compares current Delaware prohibition on written consent with proposed Texas Bylaws’ unanimous written-consent standard.
Compares Delaware and Texas special-meeting callers, the 50% shareholder threshold, and cancellation rules.
Compares charter amendment/authorized-share rules with exceptions and does not assert one universal threshold.
Compares Delaware and TBOC bylaw-amendment authority and qualifications, including possible exclusive shareholder reservation.
Lists TBOC-reserved matters that committees cannot exercise under the proposed Texas Bylaws.
Distinguishes Texas’s 20% business-combination threshold from Delaware’s 15% threshold.
Limits the forum discussion to internal entity claims and notes the proposed documents may or may not adopt a Texas forum clause.
Describes Delaware demand/futility derivative requirements.
Identifies Texas universal written demand rather than importing Delaware futility.
Identifies the 91st-day waiting rule and the rejection/irreparable-injury exceptions.
Distinguishes the new Texas business court from Delaware’s established business court and case law.
Does not state the absence of appraisal rights for this conversion and instead leaves appraisal rights unresolved.
Recognizes preservation of preconversion obligations, personal liability, and choice of law.
Attributes economic neutrality to the Special Committee’s evaluation rather than guaranteeing stock value.
Reports intended tax treatment with holder-specific and jurisdiction-specific limitations.
Recognizes that no tax opinion or IRS ruling was obtained.
Describes Texas long/short-term-interest consideration without saying fiduciary duties are eliminated.
